headline: Brent $110.4, Nasdaq fut +0.7%, Kospi +3.3%, 10y 5.11%, OAT-Bund 157bp, Oct hold 85%
stance: Equity is buying the AI prints; credit is selling the AI balance sheets. Hormuz stays shut on Tehran's word, so $110 Brent and the French spread set the 10y today.

news.head: SpaceX +8% pre-market, first profit since the June IPO
news.body: Q3 revenue $14.6bn, +161% y/y; adjusted EBITDA $8.8bn; Q4 capex guided $35-40bn. Committees formed with Tesla to explore a merger.

news.head: Netflix -6% pre-market on a $0.67 Q4 EPS guide
news.body: Consensus was $0.73. Q3 revenue $12.87bn, +12%; FY ad revenue cut to $2.7bn from $3bn. Third straight quarter of slowing growth.

news.head: Super Micro +13% pre-market on a preliminary beat
news.body: Q1 revenue flagged at $18.5-19.5bn against roughly $15bn expected, margins above guide. Micron and Intel +3.4% pre-market with it.

news.head: SoftBank 5y CDS 432bp, widest in 4 years
news.body: Up 30bp in a week on AI funding strain and a possible Allied Universal purchase. OpenAI is seeking about $30bn from holders including SoftBank.

implications: Credit prices the capex, equity the revenue: hyperscaler CDS at records the night a 161% revenue quarter lifts Nasdaq futures. The gap closes from the equity side.
Tehran says Hormuz stays shut until its terms are met; Washington calls a deal extremely difficult. $110 Brent is the base case into the Oct 28 FOMC, not the tail.

watch.head: Meta, Tesla, IBM, AT&T report after today's close
watch.body: Meta capex is the number for AI credit; Tesla gets asked about the merger committees. No US data today; jobless claims Thursday 8:30am.

watch.head: France: Moody's review Friday, budget vote postponed
watch.body: The Assembly pushed Tuesday's revenue vote; curfews remain in several cities. Europe's bank index at a four-month low Tuesday, French banks -2.5% to -3.4%.

watch.head: Hormuz: Araghchi says closed until US accepts terms
watch.body: Aired early Wednesday on Iraqi TV. Rubio: a deal is extremely difficult. Mediators' plan reportedly trades $6bn frozen funds for inspections, unconfirmed.

watch.head: Fed blackout to the Oct 28 FOMC; Michigan final Friday
watch.body: Hold priced at 85%, three hikes priced over 12 months. Chair Warsh says he does not prejudge. The following week: ECB, PCE and GDP, all Oct 29.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Brent $110.38, +1.5% (~3am ET) after a $112-to-$108.79 round trip Tuesday on a denied peace report. Tehran: Hormuz closed until its terms are met.
OAT-Bund near 157bp (~5:30am ET), 2bp off the Oct 2 high; OAT 10y 4.99%, a 24-year high. Italy-Bund 111bp, +5bp Tuesday: the spread is travelling.
10y 5.11%, flat overnight (~5:30am ET) after Tuesday's housing-starts drop took the long end lower. FOMC Oct 28: hold 85%, three hikes priced over 12 months.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13: no new extremes. Euro and sterling specs at the 1st percentile, fourth week. Background, but the French spread is testing a short that is already full.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Futures (~4am ET): Nasdaq 100 +0.7%, S&P +0.2%, Dow and Russell flat. Two AI prints after Tuesday's close did what Monday's bounce could not: Asia followed.
Kospi +3.3% after Tuesday's -3.7%; Nikkei +0.9%; Stoxx 600 +0.2% (~5am ET). Chip and memory names led each market: last week's sellers are buying back.
Tuesday: Dow +1%, best close in over a month on industrial and defense beats; S&P +0.3%; Nasdaq flat. 13% of the S&P has reported, 86% beat.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13, unchanged: Russell 2000 specs 99th percentile, third week; Nasdaq 100 97th, fourth week; VIX shorts 6th. Long futures against short vol, now with a 3% Kospi bounce behind them.

single_name.note: Inhibrx: insider-buy rule fired, filing dated Oct 14, new to the list today. Above its 200-day; days to cover 11.8. Long setup, score 5 of 5.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Hyperscaler 5y CDS set records Tuesday, one above 340bp and one above 240bp. Dealers net bought $451m of hyperscaler bonds Monday, the most since mid-September.
Holders are selling paper ahead of supply: AI-linked issuance $466bn this year against $101bn a year ago. No large-cap tech deal since August; the pipeline is Q4 and 2027.
The largest neocloud's unsecured bonds near a 15% yield, from 9.7% at the June issue; 5y CDS near 1,200bp. Buyers price a 40% five-year default probability.
sections.positioning: Dealers' HY inventory at the 28th percentile, unchanged. The hedge is single-name CDS: $140bn traded on the ten largest AI issuers in nine months, +691% y/y.
